source.prompt: Our CRM is full of duplicate contacts, how do we clean it up and stop it recurring?
source.note: real collected answer; brand, competitors and publishers are the specs the cycle was scored with

answer.text:
The fastest path is to dedupe your existing records with automated matching rules, then lock in prevention using strict data-entry rules, integration controls, and ongoing data governance.
✅ Step 1: Prepare your data before deduplication
Cleaning works best when the data is standardized.
Normalize formats: phone numbers, email casing, country codes, name capitalization.
Fill in missing fields where possible (e.g., import enrichment data).
Identify key fields that define uniqueness: email, phone, national ID, company domain, etc.
This ensures your dedupe tools match correctly instead of missing near-duplicates.
✅ Step 2: Identify and merge existing duplicates
Most CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, Dynamics, etc.) offer built‑in or add‑on dedupe tools. Use a layered approach:
Exact-match scan: email, phone, or unique ID.
Fuzzy-match scan: name similarity, company similarity, partial phone match.
Merge rules:
Keep the record with the most complete data.
Preserve activity history and deal associations.
Flag uncertain matches for manual review.
If your CRM lacks strong dedupe tools, export to Excel or Google Sheets and use:
=UNIQUE() for exact matches
Fuzzy matching add-ons (e.g., OpenRefine, Excel Fuzzy Lookup)
Then re-import clean data.
✅ Step 3: Fix the root causes so duplicates don’t return
Duplicates usually come from people, integrations, or forms. Address each:
1. Data-entry controls
Require email or phone as mandatory unique identifiers.
Enable real-time duplicate warnings (“This contact already exists”).
Use picklists instead of free text for fields like country, industry, or lead source.
2. Integration hygiene
Most duplicates come from:
Web forms
Lead providers
Marketing automation tools
Manual imports
To prevent this:
Turn on dedupe on import.
Ensure all integrations use the same unique identifier (email is best for contacts).
Block integrations from creating a new record if a match already exists.
3. User training & process
Even the best rules fail if the team ignores them.
Train staff to search before creating a new contact.
Create a simple “How to add a new contact” SOP.
Assign a data steward (even part-time) to review new records weekly.
✅ Step 4: Establish ongoing data governance
Duplicates will creep back unless you monitor them.
Run a monthly dedupe report.
Set up automated alerts for potential duplicates.
Review integration logs for suspicious spikes in new contacts.
Maintain a data dictionary so everyone uses fields consistently.
✅ Step 5: Consider automation tools (optional)
If your CRM supports it, tools like:
HubSpot Operations Hub
Salesforce Duplicate Rules + Matching Rules
Zoho DataPrep
OpenRefine
…can automate 80–90% of the work.
✅ Summary: What to do this week
Standardize your data.
Run automated dedupe scans.
Merge with clear rules.
Turn on duplicate prevention in your CRM.
Fix integrations.
Train your team.
Review monthly.
